# **CBT AI Exam Generation & Multi-Session Security Directives**

## **Executive Overview**

This document specifies the strict rules, mathematical constraints, and algorithmic directives governing the **Just-In-Time (JIT) AI Exam Generation Engine**. It ensures that exam papers compiled for multi-shift Computer-Based Tests (CBT) maintain rigorous academic standards, strict cross-session uniqueness (![][image1]), terminal-level anti-copying randomization, and cross-shift score normalization.

## **1\. Exam Blueprint & Subject Distribution Rules**

The AI pipeline must strictly enforce the target exam structure. Questions are queried and selected according to predefined subject quotas and section splits.

### **1.1 NEET UG Standard Blueprint (180 Questions / 720 Marks)**

|

| **Subject** | **Sub-Section / Domain** | **Total Questions** | **Target Easy (\~35%)** | **Target Medium (\~45%)** | **Target Hard (\~20%)** |

| **Physics** | Mechanics, Electrodynamics, Optics, Modern Physics | **45** | 16 | 20 | 9 |

| **Chemistry** | Physical, Organic, Inorganic Chemistry | **45** | 16 | 20 | 9 |

| **Biology (Botany)** | Plant Physiology, Cell Biology, Genetics, Ecology | **45** | 16 | 20 | 9 |

| **Biology (Zoology)** | Human Physiology, Reproduction, Evolution, Biotechnology | **45** | 16 | 20 | 9 |

| **TOTAL** | | **180 Questions** | **64** | **80** | **36** |

### **1.2 Sub-Topic Weightage Preservation**

For every generated paper, subject topic distribution must not deviate by more than ![][image2] from the target weightage matrix:

* **Physics:** Mechanics (![][image3]), Electrodynamics (![][image4]), Modern Physics (![][image5]), Thermodynamics (![][image5]), Optics/Waves (![][image5]).  
* **Chemistry:** Organic (![][image6]), Inorganic (![][image6]), Physical (![][image6]).  
* **Biology:** Human Physiology (![][image7]), Genetics & Evolution (![][image7]), Plant Physiology (![][image5]), Ecology (![][image5]), Cell Biology (![][image5]), Diversity/Other (![][image5]).

## **2\. Multi-Session Uniqueness Engine (![][image1] Differentiation Rule)**

For competitive exams held across multiple shifts (e.g., Morning and Evening shifts across multiple days), papers must be sufficiently distinct to prevent leakages and ensure fairness.

       \[ Global Question Bank (MongoDB Encrypted) \]  
                           │  
                           ▼  
  \[ Query Pool: Exclude Question IDs from Previous Shift Log \]  
                           │  
                           ▼  
  \[ Check Uniqueness Metric: Unseen Questions \>= 80% \] ──► (Fail) ──► \[ Swap & Re-Query \]  
                           │  
                           │ (Pass: Overlap \<= 20%)  
                           ▼  
  \[ Verify Allowed 20% Overlap uses Parametric Variants \]  
                           │  
                           ▼  
  \[ Deliver Final Session Master Payload to Redis \]

### **2.1 The 80% Differentiation Constraint**

For any given session ![][image8] within an exam cycle:

1. ![][image9]**Unseen ID Quota (![][image1]):** At least ![][image10] (![][image11] out of ![][image12] questions) of the questions in session ![][image8] must have **never been used** in any previous session (![][image13]) during the same exam cycle.  
2. **Parametric Variant Rule for Overlapping Items (![][image14]):** The remaining ![][image7] (![][image15] questions or fewer) that test identical core concepts must be **parametric variants** (e.g., modified numerical constants, inverted chemical reaction parameters, or rephrased scenario conditions).

### **2.2 Global Session History Logging**

After an exam session completes, all used question IDs are appended to the used\_questions\_registry in MongoDB:

{  
  "exam\_year": 2026,  
  "session\_id": "DAY\_01\_SHIFT\_01\_MORNING",  
  "generated\_at": "2026-07-24T08:45:00Z",  
  "question\_ids": \["q\_phy\_104", "q\_chem\_892", "q\_bot\_332", "..."\]  
}

When generating paper ![][image8], the Python FastAPI microservice injects the question\_ids list from previous shifts into the MongoDB $nin (Not In) filter query.

## **3\. In-Session Terminal Series Randomization (Anti-Copying Rules)**

To eliminate side-by-side cheating in exam labs without creating multiple static master papers, the system enforces **Deterministic Terminal-Level Seeded Shuffling**.

Master Session Paper (180 Questions)  
                 │  
                 ├──► Terminal 01 (Roll: 101\) ──► Seed \= SHA256("EXAM\_01" \+ "101") ──► Order: Q41, Q12, Q89...  
                 │  
                 └──► Terminal 02 (Roll: 102\) ──► Seed \= SHA256("EXAM\_01" \+ "102") ──► Order: Q89, Q04, Q12...

### **3.1 Question Order Permutation**

* Each candidate terminal calculates a unique cryptographic seed:  
* ![][image16]The React client executes a **Seeded Fisher-Yates Algorithm** using this seed to reorder the 180 questions locally in RAM.  
* **Result:** Candidate A at Terminal 1 and Candidate B at Terminal 2 sit next to each other, but Candidate A's Question \#1 is Candidate B's Question \#41.

### **3.2 Option Index Permutation**

* For every multiple-choice question, the four option choices (![][image17]) are also shuffled deterministically using the terminal seed.  
* **Result:** Even if two candidates manage to see the same question text on screen, Option (A) on Terminal 1 corresponds to Option (C) on Terminal 2\.

## **4\. Difficulty & Cognitive Balance Rules**

Every session paper must follow an identical cognitive difficulty distribution to maintain uniform standards across all test days.

### **4.1 Difficulty Classification Matrix**

| **Category** | **Definition** | **Target Ratio** | **Marks Allocation** |

| **Easy** | Single-step formula application / direct factual recall. | **35%** (![][image18]) | \~252 Marks |

| **Medium** | Multi-step calculation / concept synthesis / diagram analysis. | **45%** (![][image18]) | \~324 Marks |

| **Hard** | Novel problem context / multi-concept integration / rigorous math. | **20%** (![][image18]) | \~144 Marks |

### **4.2 LangChain \+ Gemini Audit Guidelines**

During the JIT 15-minute generation window, the Gemini Auditor Agent checks candidate questions against the following rules:

1. **Ambiguity Rejection:** Reject any question where two options could be argued as correct.  
2. **Semantic Redundancy Rejection:** If two candidate questions test the exact same formula (e.g., ![][image19]) using the same steps, discard one and request a replacement from the buffer.  
3. **Option Distractor Quality:** Reject questions where incorrect options (distractors) are obviously invalid or grammatically mismatched with the prompt.

## **5\. Cross-Shift Normalization Rules**

Because different sessions feature ![][image1] different questions, slight variations in raw paper difficulty are statistically inevitable. To ensure total candidate equity, final results are processed using **Equi-percentile Normalization**.

### **5.1 Percentile Calculation Formula**

For candidate ![][image20] in session ![][image8], the percentile score ![][image21] is calculated as:

![][image22]Where:

* ![][image23] \= Total number of candidates in session ![][image8] who scored **less than or equal to** candidate ![][image20]'s raw score.  
* ![][image24] \= Total number of candidates who appeared in session ![][image8].

### **5.2 Merit List Rule**

* **All AIR (All India Ranks)** or merit positions are computed using the **Percentile Scores** rounded to 7 decimal places, **never the raw marks**.  
* Raw marks are used strictly inside an individual session to establish relative rank within that shift.

## **6\. Cryptographic & Operational Constraints**

1. **In-Memory Decryption Window:** Raw question text must remain encrypted in MongoDB (AES-256-GCM) and decrypted **only inside FastAPI RAM** 15 minutes prior to session launch (![][image25]).  
2. **Redis TTL Limit:** The final audited master paper stored in Redis must carry a strict Time-To-Live (TTL):  
3. ![][image26]**RAM Memory Flush Directive:** Once the audited master paper is encrypted and sent to Redis, FastAPI must explicitly run del decrypted\_pool and invoke gc.collect() to wipe plaintext data from server RAM.  
4. **Audit Hash Link:** Every generated session paper is hashed using SHA-256 and recorded in the MongoDB audit log to verify payload integrity post-exam.

## **7\. Execution Checklist for AI Pipeline**

| **Step** | **Responsible Layer** | **Rule Enforced** |

| **1\. Aggregation Query** | PyMongo / FastAPI | Fetch 1.5x buffer matching subject counts & excluding previous shift IDs (![][image27] filter). |

| **2\. Decryption** | crypto\_utils.py | Decrypt buffer strictly in RAM using MASTER\_ENCRYPTION\_KEY. |

| **3\. LangChain Audit** | Gemini 2.5 Flash | Select exactly 180 questions, balance 35/45/20 difficulty, remove semantic duplicates. |

| **4\. Pydantic Validation** | Pydantic Schema | Validate exact count compliance (45 Phy / 45 Chem / 45 Bot / 45 Zoo). |

| **5\. Session Encryption** | crypto\_utils.py | Re-encrypt final 180-question master paper payload. |

| **6\. Redis Caching** | Redis Cache | Save under exam:{exam\_id}:master with TTL \= Exam Duration \+ 15m. |

| **7\. Seeded Client Render** | React Frontend | Apply Seeded Fisher-Yates shuffle per candidate terminal using student roll number. |
